content: P0322 - Knock Sensor Circuit Low Input. The knock sensor voltage is below the expected range. Causes include a shorted signal wire, failed sensor, or open circuit. Inspect wiring and sensor resistance.
P0323 - Knock Sensor Circuit High Input. The knock sensor voltage is above the expected range. Causes include an open signal wire or a failed sensor. Inspect wiring and ground circuit.

P0324 - Knock Sensor Circuit Input Range/Performance Problem. The knock sensor signal is out of expected range. Causes include a failing sensor, damaged wiring, or incorrect torque on sensor. Inspect sensor and wiring.

P0329 - Knock Sensor Circuit High Input (Bank 2). The knock sensor voltage for bank 2 is above the expected range. Causes include an open signal wire or a failed sensor. Inspect wiring and ground connections.

P0330 - Knock Sensor Circuit Malfunction (Bank 2). The knock sensor for bank 2 has an open, short, or poor connection. Causes include damaged wiring, failed sensor, or a bad ECM driver. Inspect wiring and sensor resistance.

P0331 - Knock Sensor Circuit Range/Performance Problem (Bank 2). The knock sensor signal for bank 2 is out of expected range. Causes include a failing sensor, damaged wiring, or incorrect torque on sensor. Inspect sensor and wiring.

P0332 - Knock Sensor Circuit Low Input (Bank 2). The knock sensor voltage for bank 2 is below the expected range. Causes include a shorted signal wire, failed sensor, or open circuit. Inspect wiring and sensor.

P0333 - Knock Sensor Circuit High Input (Bank 2). The knock sensor voltage for bank 2 is above the expected range. Causes include an open signal wire or a failed sensor. Inspect wiring and ground circuit.

P0334 - Knock Sensor Circuit Intermittent Malfunction (Bank 2). The knock sensor signal for bank 2 is intermittent. Causes include damaged wiring, loose connector, or a failing sensor. Inspect wiring and connector security.
